description:
pkix-lint/src/deviation.rs lines 529-536: DeviationStore::add asserts that deviation.justification is non-empty and deviation.authorized_by is non-empty, panicking if either is empty. These are assert! (not debug_assert!), so they fire in release builds. If a Deviation is constructed from deserialized JSON (e.g., loading a stored deviation store file), a malformed or adversarially crafted file with empty strings would panic the process rather than returning an error.

The doc comment says "Panics if..." which documents the behaviour, but from a safety standpoint: (a) the panic is reachable from a public API method with externally-supplied input if Deviation can be deserialized, (b) DeviatedFinding has serde derives, and (c) the module doc shows loading stored evidence packs. The correct fix is to return a new DeviationAddError variant (e.g., EmptyField) instead of panicking, or at minimum document this clearly as a programming-error-only panic with a note that callers loading from external sources must validate fields before calling add.
title: P1: DeviationStore::add panics on untrusted data (justification/authorized_by from deserialized Deviation)
